paragraphs: Shimon ben Tarfon. (A tanna mentioned in a baraita.)

Two legal teachings of his remain with us, as in [Shevuot 47b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.47b.3-4). He said: “This teaches that the oath takes effect upon both of them.” He also said there: “Where is the warning against one who acts as a procurer for an adulterer? Scripture says, ‘You shall not commit adultery’—read as ‘You shall not cause adultery.’”[^1][^2]

He also said there: “‘And you murmured in your tents’—you scouted [the land] and maligned [God] in the tent of the Omnipresent.” He also said there: “Draw near to one who is oiled, and be oiled yourself.”[^3]

notes.text: Hyman introduces two legal teachings and then adds two further sayings. All four occur together at Shevuot 47b:3–6.
The wordplay is לא תנאף / לא תנאיף, “do not commit adultery” / “do not cause adultery.” Rashi on Shevuot 47b:4:1 explains the person’s role as an agent arranging women for the adulterer.

The bracketed objects follow Rashi on Shevuot 47b:5:1–2: “you scouted” refers to the land, and “you maligned” to the Omnipresent who caused His presence to dwell among them. “In the tent of the Omnipresent” follows the Hebrew wording. Rashi on 47b:6:1 explains the oil proverb through contact with someone covered in oil and through the Euphrates gaining importance from its association with the Land of Israel.
